To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• Ontology building is a complex task that requires the use of a methodology, tools, and languages, which should be integrated in a workbench to facilitate the development and management of ontologies.
the main methodologies, languages and tools for building ontologies are: METHONTOLOGY, ONTOLOG and the Ontology Development Kit (ODK).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the design of an ontology development environment that supports the development of ontologies, and (2) the design of a methodological framework that guides the ontology developer in this task.

the development of a methodology for the construction of ontologies, the development of a tool to support the methodology, the definition of a formal ontology language and its implementation, as well as with the definition of a mapping between this language and other languages.
developing and using ontologies for knowledge management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current state-of-the-art in ontology technology is not yet mature enough to support the development of large-scale ontologies, but it is definitely good enough for the development of small and middle-sized ontologies, and it is also good enough for the integration of small ontologies into larger ones.
there is a wide variety of methodologies, tools, and languages for building and managing ontologies, which are still under development and improvement.

(1) the methodologies and tools are more mature than the languages, (2) there are many languages and tools, but few methodologies, (3) the methodologies and languages do not have a clear separation between the different phases of the ontology building process, (4) the languages do not have the same expressivity, and (5) there are no tools to support the different phases of ontology building, and there are no translations among the languages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ontology engineering community has made a great effort in providing a variety of tools and languages for ontology development.
we have reviewed and compared the most relevant methodologies, tools and ontology languages for building ontological engineering applications.
we are in a position to say that the ontology engineering field has matured enough to provide the necessary technology components for building ontologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state of the art is not yet good enough to provide a common workbench for ontology engineering.
there is an important gap between the methodologies, languages and tools for building ontologies, and that this gap should be closed.
there is a wide variety of methodologies, tools and ontological representation languages, and that they are complementary.
